weightingMethod: equal-per-objective-count — Cisco publishes no official per-domain scoring weight for this exam as of ingestion time

objectives.title: Identify the fundamental conceptual building blocks of networks.
contentExamples: TCP/IP model, OSI model, frames and packets, addressing

objectives.title: Differentiate between bandwidth and throughput.
contentExamples: Latency, delay, speed test vs. Iperf

objectives.title: Differentiate between LAN, WAN, MAN, CAN, PAN, and WLAN.
contentExamples: Identify and illustrate common physical and logical network topologies

objectives.title: Compare and contrast cloud and on-premises applications and services.
contentExamples: Public, private, hybrid, SaaS, PaaS, IaaS, remote work/hybrid work

objectives.title: Describe common network applications and protocols.
contentExamples: TCP vs. UDP (connection-oriented vs. connectionless), FTP, SFTP, TFTP, HTTP, HTTPS, DHCP, DNS, ICMP, NTP

objectives.title: Compare and contrast private addresses and public addresses.
contentExamples: Address classes, NAT concepts

objectives.title: Identify IPv4 addresses and subnet formats.
contentExamples: Subnet concepts, Subnet Calculator, slash notation, and subnet mask; broadcast domain

objectives.title: Identify IPv6 addresses and prefix formats.
contentExamples: Types of addresses, prefix concepts

objectives.title: Identify cables and connectors commonly used in local area networks.
contentExamples: Cable types: fiber, copper, twisted pair; Connector types: coax, RJ-45, RJ-11, fiber connector types

objectives.title: Differentiate between Wi-Fi, cellular, and wired network technologies.
contentExamples: Copper, including sources of interference; fiber; wireless, including 802.11 (unlicensed, 2.4GHz, 5GHz, 6GHz), cellular (licensed), sources of interference

objectives.title: Describe endpoint devices.
contentExamples: Internet of Things (IoT) devices, computers, mobile devices, IP Phone, printer, server

objectives.title: Demonstrate how to set up and check network connectivity on Windows, Linux, Mac OS, Android, and Apple iOS.
contentExamples: Networking utilities on Windows, Linux, Android, and Apple operating systems; how to run troubleshooting commands; wireless client settings (SSID, authentication, WPA mode)

objectives.title: Identify the status lights on a Cisco device when given instruction by an engineer.
contentExamples: Link light color and status (blinking or solid)

objectives.title: Use a network diagram provided by an engineer to attach the appropriate cables.
contentExamples: Patch cables, switches and routers, small topologies, power, rack layout

objectives.title: Identify the various ports on network devices.
contentExamples: Console port, serial port, fiber port, Ethernet ports, SFPs, USB port, PoE

objectives.title: Explain basic routing concepts.
contentExamples: Default gateway, layer 2 vs. layer 3 switches, local network vs. remote network

objectives.title: Explain basic switching concepts.
contentExamples: MAC address tables, MAC address filtering, VLAN

objectives.title: Demonstrate effective troubleshooting methodologies and help desk best practices, including ticketing, documentation, and information gathering.
contentExamples: Policies and procedures, accurate and complete documentation, prioritization

objectives.title: Perform a packet capture with Wireshark and save it to a file.
contentExamples: Purpose of using a packet analyzer, saving and opening a .pcap file

objectives.title: Run basic diagnostic commands and interpret the results.
contentExamples: ping, ipconfig/ifconfig/ip, tracert/traceroute, nslookup; recognize how firewalls can influence the result

objectives.title: Differentiate between different ways to access and collect data about network devices.
contentExamples: Remote access (RDP, SSH, telnet), VPN, terminal emulators, Console, Network Management Systems, cloud-managed network (Meraki), scripts

objectives.title: Run basic show commands on a Cisco network device.
contentExamples: show run, show cdp neighbors, show ip interface brief, show ip route, show version, show inventory, show switch, show mac address-table, show interface, show interface x, show interface status; privilege levels; command help and auto-complete

objectives.title: Describe how firewalls operate to filter traffic.
contentExamples: Firewalls (blocked ports and protocols); rules deny or permit access

objectives.title: Describe foundational security concepts.
contentExamples: Confidentiality, integrity, and availability (CIA); authentication, authorization, and accounting (AAA); Multifactor Authentication (MFA); encryption, certificates, and password complexity; identity stores/databases (Active Directory); threats and vulnerabilities; spam, phishing, malware, and denial of service

objectives.title: Configure basic wireless security on a home router (WPAx).
contentExamples: WPA, WPA2, WPA3; choosing between Personal and Enterprise; wireless security concepts
